issue.title: [P1][GC] Reserve stable virtual-address backing for heap spaces and the handle table
issue.body:
## Context

The current Throughput old-space backing and handle table are Go slices that can relocate when they grow. Generated code must reload bases and lengths through the native view, and old-space growth can allocate and copy the entire backing. Stable reserved address ranges would remove those copies and simplify native access.

## Scope

### Stable heap backing

- [ ] Reserve the configured maximum Throughput heap as virtual address space when supported.
- [ ] Commit/decommit physical pages lazily as allocation and reclamation require.
- [ ] Keep nursery, old, large-object, and future region bases stable for the collector lifetime.
- [ ] Preserve bounded configured limits and explicit exhaustion behavior.
- [ ] Add a portable fallback for platforms/builds without the required mapping APIs.

### Stable handle backing

- [ ] Reserve a bounded virtual range for the handle table.
- [ ] Commit handle pages lazily.
- [ ] Preserve handle index zero as invalid/null protection.
- [ ] Publish stable table base/capacity through the versioned native ABI.
- [ ] Avoid slice reallocation and view refresh solely because a handle was appended.

### Native integration

- [ ] Patch or cache stable bases at instance setup where safe.
- [ ] Remove hot-path pointer reloads that exist only because Go backing can move.
- [ ] Preserve serialization, `Close`, ownership, and native execution synchronization.
- [ ] Ensure no Go pointer is stored in guest-visible state.

### Measurement

- [ ] Report old-space backing-copy bytes eliminated.
- [ ] Measure allocation latency at each commit boundary.
- [ ] Measure RSS, committed bytes, reserved address space, page faults, and JIT instruction changes.
- [ ] Test small heaps where virtual reservation overhead must remain negligible.

## Correctness gates

- [ ] Guard against address/length overflow and mapping failure.
- [ ] Verify stale native views cannot access decommitted or closed backing.
- [ ] Test guard-page and explicit bounds products on linux/amd64, linux/arm64, and Darwin/arm64 where supported.

## Acceptance criteria

- Normal old-space growth performs no full backing copy.
- Normal handle growth does not relocate the native handle table.
- Existing hard heap limits and fail-closed behavior remain exact.
issue.display_title: [P1][GC] Reserve stable virtual-address backing for heap spaces and the handle table

issue.title: [P1][GC] Prototype a 16-byte hot handle and compact object headers
issue.body:
## Context

The current native handle stride is 20 bytes and objects carry a 16-byte header. Size and several flags are duplicated or derivable. The fixed handle-plus-header cost is therefore large for small WasmGC objects, and the 20-byte stride requires multiplication during handle resolution.

## Scope

### Hot handle layout

- [ ] Prototype a 16-byte handle record with fields equivalent to region/offset, logical object size, canonical type or layout ID, and packed metadata.
- [ ] Pack space, generation/age, size-class/region class, and required flags into the metadata word.
- [ ] Move allocator-only `allocSize` into span/page/region metadata.
- [ ] Move remembered/card membership into bitmaps or side metadata rather than every handle.
- [ ] Derive allocation size from size class when possible.
- [ ] Use shift/scaled addressing for handle resolution.

### Object header

- [ ] Remove duplicate object size from either the handle or object header.
- [ ] Derive pointer-free and large-object state from type/region metadata.
- [ ] Keep mark and age state outside guest object bytes.
- [ ] Prototype an 8-byte header carrying only per-object dynamic data such as array length/auxiliary state.
- [ ] Evaluate header-free structs where type/size live entirely in the handle.
- [ ] Preserve exact array length, exception/object auxiliary data, and all layout alignment.

### Safety and compatibility

- [ ] Version the native collector ABI and reject incompatible persisted artifacts.
- [ ] Preserve `RefEq` and stable handle identity across relocation.
- [ ] Retain test-only stale-reference cookies/generations where needed without changing guest equality.

### Measurement

- [ ] Report metadata bytes/object and metadata bytes/live payload byte.
- [ ] Measure handle-resolution instructions, cache misses, collector scan bandwidth, JIT bytes, and linked bytes.
- [ ] Compare at least `16-byte handle + 8-byte header` and `16-byte handle + header-free struct` designs.

## Acceptance criteria

- The retained layout materially reduces metadata/cache traffic on small-object workloads.
- Handle resolution is no slower on amd64 or arm64.
- No semantic, codec, ownership, or stale-reference regression is introduced.
issue.display_title: [P1][GC] Prototype a 16-byte hot handle and compact object headers

issue.title: [P2][GC] Design and implement a stable-handle Immix-style old generation
issue.body:
## Context

Wago's 32-bit guest references are stable handles rather than raw object pointers. This makes selective old-space evacuation unusually cheap: copy object bytes and update one handle entry without rewriting every heap reference. An Immix-style mark-region old generation is the strongest long-term fit for throughput, locality, fragmentation control, and compact implementation.

## Scope

### Region/block/line design

- [ ] Define coarse old-space blocks/regions and fine-grained allocation lines.
- [ ] Maintain per-region object-start, mark, card, generation, occupancy, and free-line metadata.
- [ ] Allocate contiguously through free line runs using bump cursors.
- [ ] Separate or classify pointer-free regions to reduce tracing work.
- [ ] Give large objects dedicated independently reclaimable/ageable regions.

### Mark and sweep

- [ ] Pack mark state in bitmaps and clear logically with polarity/epochs.
- [ ] Trace using precomputed type scan programs.
- [ ] Group marking work by page/region for locality.
- [ ] Scan dense reference arrays in bounded chunks.
- [ ] Sweep lazily by region and immediately convert empty regions into bump arenas.
- [ ] Maintain live-byte/line counts during marking.

### Selective evacuation

- [ ] Rank sparse regions by live bytes, connectivity/card cost, and evacuation benefit.
- [ ] Copy selected live objects into destination regions.
- [ ] Update only stable handle metadata after each object is completely copied.
- [ ] Never retain a raw object address across a safepoint or evacuation boundary.
- [ ] Reclaim evacuated regions transactionally.
- [ ] Age surviving young large-object regions in place where safe.

### Memory return

- [ ] Decommit or `madvise` long-idle empty regions on supported platforms.
- [ ] Preserve virtual reservation and hard heap limits.

## Staging

1. Region allocator and metadata behind an experimental profile.
2. Mark/sweep without evacuation.
3. Selective evacuation with shadow verification.
4. Replace the current old generation only after sustained evidence.

## Measurement

- Long-running fragmented heaps, sparse and dense graphs, low/high liveness, large objects, and mixed object sizes.
- Full-GC pause distribution, mark bandwidth, sweep cost, evacuated bytes, handle updates, fragmentation, cache misses, RSS, and mutator throughput.

## Acceptance criteria

- Old-space allocation and reclamation have bounded metadata behavior.
- Fragmentation remains controlled over long randomized workloads.
- Evacuation updates stable handles rather than rewriting the complete object graph.
- The retained implementation improves full-GC throughput and memory efficiency without unacceptable linked-size growth.
issue.display_title: [P2][GC] Design and implement a stable-handle Immix-style old generation

issue.title: [P3][GC] Add parallel and concurrent collection only behind measured heap-size thresholds
issue.body:
## Context

Wago should not begin with a G1/ZGC/Shenandoah-scale concurrent design. Concurrency becomes useful only after exact roots, card-driven minor collection, compact metadata, stable regions, and efficient single-threaded collection are complete. This issue records the explicitly deferred path and its admission criteria.

## Required prerequisites

- [ ] Collector-cycle telemetry and pause distributions are available.
- [ ] Exact root maps cover the target generated workloads.
- [ ] Real card/root remembered sets are collection inputs.
- [ ] Mark state uses packed epoch/polarity metadata.
- [ ] Stable heap/handle backing and region metadata exist.
- [ ] Mutation barriers are already minimized and proven.

## Staged scope

### Phase 1: background sweeping

- [ ] Sweep reclaimed old regions/spans outside the mutator pause where safe.
- [ ] Preserve deterministic allocation fallback when background work is unavailable.

### Phase 2: parallel stop-the-world marking

- [ ] Enable only above measured live-heap/object thresholds.
- [ ] Use per-worker local mark queues with work stealing.
- [ ] Group work by region/page and use bounded queue-transfer synchronization.
- [ ] Keep the single-mutator/small-heap path worker-free.

### Phase 3: parallel evacuation

- [ ] Give workers private survivor/old destination chunks.
- [ ] Publish copied objects through stable handles only after complete initialization.
- [ ] Preserve transactional failure semantics.

### Phase 4: concurrent marking

- [ ] Add safepoint handshakes, phase transitions, and a proven incremental-update or SATB barrier.
- [ ] Keep foreground young collection compatible with background old marking.
- [ ] Bound remark work and report p99/max latency.

### Explicit non-goals unless later evidence demands them

- [ ] Do not add colored pointers.
- [ ] Do not add a load barrier to every object access.
- [ ] Do not implement concurrent relocation by default.
- [ ] Do not introduce a global process-wide collector.

## Measurement

- Compare one, two, four, and available-core worker counts.
- Report pause distributions, total CPU, wall time, cache misses, synchronization, mutator throughput, RSS, and linked-size growth.
- Demonstrate a clear benefit at large heaps and no regression for small/default workloads.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every phase lands separately behind thresholds and temporary A/B controls.
- Parallelism is disabled when startup/synchronization costs exceed measured benefit.
- Concurrent machinery can be excluded from minimal/Tiny products at build time.
issue.display_title: [P3][GC] Add parallel and concurrent collection only behind measured heap-size thresholds
